slides.heading: Reception — Autumn 1, Week 3
slides.sub: New sounds taught directly, practised and applied in words, captions and the matching decodable book.

slides.heading: Mon
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "i" (/ɪ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="igloo" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="igloo"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Iggy the raindrop drips off the leaf tip in a hurry — 'i, i, i' — plip, plip, plip.

character.name: Iggy
character.blurb: Iggy is a tiny, speedy raindrop who never sits still for long, always dripping quickly from leaf to leaf.

slides.pronunciation_note: A short, quick sound — 'i' as in 'sit', not the long letter name 'eye'.
slides.formation_cue: Start at the top of the small letters. Pull straight down and finish on the line. Lift, and add a dot above.
slides.formation_rhyme: Short line down, dot on top.
slides.action: Give one quick, tiny tap on top of your head with a fingertip, like a drop landing, saying a short 'i'.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="igloo" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="igloo"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.tip: On its own this letter keeps its short /a/ sound, as in 'cat'. The tricky part: in a sentence we say it quickly and softly, like 'uh' — 'a cat' sounds like 'uh cat'.

slides.heading: Tue
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "n" (/n/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="nest" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="nest"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Nettie the nest hums softly as her baby birds settle down to sleep — 'n, n, n'.

character.name: Nettie
character.blurb: Nettie is a cosy woven nest tucked into a hedge, with one twig always sticking out at a funny angle.

slides.pronunciation_note: A gentle hum through the nose with the tongue behind the top teeth — 'n', not 'nuh'.
slides.formation_cue: Start at the top of the small letters. Pull straight down, go back up the same line, then over in a hump and down. Finish on the line.
slides.action: Cup both hands together in front of your chest like a small nest and hum a gentle 'nnn', tongue tip behind your top teeth.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="nest" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="nest"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.heading: Wed
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "m" (/m/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="mug" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="mug"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Milo the mushroom hums happily under the shady tree all day long — 'mmm, mmm'.

character.name: Milo
character.blurb: Milo is a round, spotty mushroom who loves cool, shady corners of the garden and hums to himself all day.

slides.pronunciation_note: A closed-lip hum held for a moment — 'mmm', not 'muh'.
slides.formation_cue: Start at the top of the small letters. Pull straight down, go back up, over in a hump and down, back up and over in a second hump and down. Finish on the line.
slides.action: Press your lips together and hum a long 'mmm' while patting both cheeks gently, like Milo humming to himself.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="mug" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="mug"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.heading: Thu
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "d" (/d/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="dog" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="dog"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Dara the duckling dips her beak into the pond three times — 'd, d, d'.

character.name: Dara
character.blurb: Dara is a bright golden duckling who loves dipping her beak into the pond to look for pondweed.

slides.pronunciation_note: A firm, quick tap of the tongue just behind the top teeth — 'd', not 'duh'.
slides.formation_cue: Start at the top right of a small round shape. Curve round to the left and back up to where you started, keep going straight up to make a tall line, then come straight back down it without lifting. Finish on the line.
slides.formation_rhyme: Round like c, then tall and down.
slides.action: Dip your head forward and down quickly, like Dara dipping for pondweed, saying 'd, d'.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="dog" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="dog"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.heading: Fri
slides.objective: Revisit everything taught this week, read the matched decodable book, and check how securely it has been learned.
